title: Nut-Free Sugar Cookie Cupcakes
shortDescription: Soft vanilla cupcakes that taste like frosted sugar cookies, ready in 25 minutes of prep and 18 minutes of baking, always nut-free.
description: These cupcakes taste like a frosted sugar cookie in cake form. I tested this batch in my own kitchen to get that buttery, slightly almond-free vanilla flavor right.
ingredients: 1/2 cup unsalted butter, softened, for frosting
Rainbow sprinkles, nut-free brand, for topping
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F. Line a 12 cup muffin pan with paper liners.
Whisk flour, baking powder, and salt in a bowl. Set aside.
Beat butter and sugar together for 3 minutes until pale and fluffy.
Add eggs one at a time, beating well after each. Mix in vanilla.
Add flour mix in three parts, alternating with milk and sour cream. Mix just until smooth.
Divide batter evenly among liners, filling each about two thirds full.
Bake 16 to 18 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean. Cool in pan 5 minutes, then move to a rack.
Beat frosting butter until smooth. Add powdered sugar in two batches with the milk. Beat 2 more minutes until fluffy.
Pipe frosting high on cooled cupcakes and finish with sprinkles right away.
tips: Check every label. Buy sprinkles, sanding sugar, and vanilla marked nut-free to keep this batch fully safe.
Room temperature eggs and butter blend smoother and give a lighter crumb.
Chill piped cupcakes for 10 minutes before serving so the frosting holds its shape.
Swap in almond-free vanilla bean paste for a deeper cookie flavor without any nut risk.

faq.question: Why do these cupcakes taste like sugar cookies?
faq.answer: The extra vanilla, sour cream, and simple butter frosting mimic the flavor of a frosted sugar cookie. There is no cookie mix involved, just the right ratio of vanilla to butter.

faq.question: Are these cupcakes really nut-free?
faq.answer: Yes, every ingredient in this recipe is naturally nut-free. Just double check your sprinkles and vanilla extract brand, since some are processed in facilities with nuts.

faq.question: Can I make these ahead for a holiday party?
faq.answer: Bake the cupcakes up to 2 days ahead and store them unfrosted at room temperature in an airtight container. Frost the morning of your party for the freshest look.

faq.question: Can I use a boxed cake mix instead?
faq.answer: Yes, a nut-free vanilla box mix works if you add 1/2 teaspoon extra vanilla extract and swap the water for milk. The homemade version has a firmer, more cookie-like crumb though.

conclusion: These cupcakes bring sugar cookie flavor to a party tray without any nut worry. Bake a batch for your next holiday cluster and watch them disappear first.
